newsitem.title: USA: Meat groups ask USDA for export report extension.
newsitem.headline: Meat groups ask USDA for export report extension.

text.p: Two major meat industry groups have written the U.S. Agriculture Department asking for a 30-day extension of the comment period on USDA's proposal to release weekly export sales data on beef, pork and poultry.

In a letter dated Nov. 22, the National Cattlemen's Beef Association (NCBA) applauded the department for addressing the issue and requested a 30-day extension so it could get "broad-based input" from its members at their annual convention in Kansas City at the end of January.
"The advance notice requests industry input on a number of issues, some of which may be controversial and many that are not specifically addressed by current NCBA policy," the cattlemen wrote.

In a letter dated Dec. 11, the American Meat Institute seconded the cattlemen's request saying an extension would give the industry time "to become more familiar with the issues and implications of the various approaches USDA might consider...

"USDA's Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking on export sales reporting has raised serious concerns among AMI's member companies about competitive business interests that could be compromised by some aspects of this ANPR, threatening the overall welfare of all sectors of the U.S. livestock and meat industry should USDA not proceeds carefully should USDA not proceed carefully in the export reporting area," AMI wrote.
USDA published the export sales report proposal in the Federal Register last month and set a Jan. 13 deadline for comments. Written comments on the proposal are available to the public.
